name: Talondo'
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Only Valkama 1987 sociolinguistic survey of Kabupaten Mamuju; no phonology/grammar of Talondo' exists

sources.citation: Sulawesi Language Alliance (David Mead), language page 'Talondo'' (sulang.org/languages/talondo), archived copy via web.archive.org (2022).
sources.note: Nothing; gives location, tentative classification (Sa'dan Toraja subgroup vs Seko), population 1,200 (2011), and references Valkama 1987, Friberg & Laskowske 1989, van der Veen 1929.

sources.citation: Kurniawati, Wati. 2020. Struktur frasa, klausa, dan kalimat bahasa Talondo. Sirok Bastra 8(1): 109-122. doi:10.37671/sb.v8i1.207
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing (syntax). p.111 summarises Palupi 2018:60 — 8 vowel phonemes, 2 long vowels, 11 diphthongs, 17 consonants, 9 consonant sequences, 5 syllable types, mostly no clusters — with no mention of tekanan/stress.

sources.citation: Nugroho, Mardi. 2017. Pembentukan kata dalam bahasa Talondo. Sirok Bastra 5(2): 123-129. doi:10.37671/sb.v5i2.102
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing (word formation: affixation, reduplication, compounding). Cites the unpublished Badan Bahasa report Palupi, Siregar & Aritonang 2014 'Fonologi dan Leksikon Bahasa Talondo' as covering vowel/consonant phonemes, distribution, long vs short vowels, consonant sequences.

sources.citation: Aritonang, Buha. 2016. Kriteria vitalitas bahasa Talondo. Ranah: Jurnal Kajian Bahasa 5(1): 8-24. doi:10.26499/rnh.v5i1.34

sources.citation: Friberg, Timothy & Thomas V. Laskowske. 1989. South Sulawesi languages, 1989. In J. N. Sneddon (ed.), Studies in Sulawesi linguistics, part 1 (NUSA 31), 1-17. Jakarta: Universitas Katolik Atma Jaya.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. p.8 (scanned, no text layer): Talondo' unknown to Grimes & Grimes, 80% lexically similar to Kalumpang but not understood by Kalumpang speakers 'in part due to phonological differences, e.g. h versus r'; possibly genetically Seko (Panasuan) with heavy Kalumpang borrowing.

sources.citation: Valkama, Kari. 1987. Kabupaten Mamuju. In Timothy Friberg (ed.), UNHAS-SIL South Sulawesi sociolinguistic surveys 1983-1987 (Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 5), 99-117. Ujung Pandang: Summer Institute of Linguistics.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Talondo' treated pp.106-109 only for location, 80% lexical similarity with Kalumpang, and non-intelligibility reports; 'Residue' lists its status vs Kalumpang as an open question.

sources.citation: Palupi, Dian. 2018. Deskripsi fonologi dan leksikon bahasa Talondo: langkah awal pendokumentasian bahasa daerah. Prosiding Seminar Nasional Bahasa dan Sastra 2017. Bandarlampung: Kantor Bahasa Provinsi Lampung (cited at p.60 by Kurniawati 2020).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only published phonological description of Talondo' (8 V, 2 long V, 11 diphthongs, 17 C, 5 syllable types per Kurniawati's summary); a Badan Bahasa 'sistem fonologi' write-up normally includes a suprasegmental/tekanan paragraph.

sources.citation: Palupi, Dian, Marida G. Siregar & Buha Aritonang. 2014. Bahasa terancam punah: fonologi dan leksikon bahasa Talondo. Laporan penelitian, Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa, Jakarta.
